title: Synthesize derivative cancellation from positive auxiliary moments
statement: Let A=-fprime(E0), B=-fsecond(E0)/2,C=-fthird(E0)/6. Necessarily mu0=g*A-1>=0,mu2=g*C>=0 and mu0*mu2>=mu1^2, mu1=g*B. For upper poles beyond Emax, T=1/(Emax-E0), strict conditions mu0>0,0<mu1<T*mu0,mu1^2<=mu0*mu2<T*mu0*mu1 give an at-most-two-atom construction. Positivity of the complete Hamiltonian is separate.

requires: Specified scalar one-port lossless continuum, finite positive-energy positive-residue emitter-side auxiliary modes with no pole at E0, ordinary real self-energy derivatives and a declared phase frame. The constructive upper-pole criterion includes strict support inequalities; full Hamiltonian positivity is checked separately.

body: Set s_i=1/(Omega_i-E0),w_i=|V_i|^2*s_i^2. Cauchy-Schwarz gives the Hankel test. At equality use s=mu1/mu0,w=mu0; otherwise choose small positive s1 and s2=(mu2-mu1*s1)/(mu1-mu0*s1),w2=(mu1-mu0*s1)/(s2-s1),w1=mu0-w2. Then Omega_i=E0+1/s_i,V_i^2=w_i/s_i^2 and H cancels D(E0). For positive A,B,C and AC>B^2 this yields gmin=C/(AC-B^2); the hard-band threshold and rank-one pole are source-specific applications of established moment mathematics.
